submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on a token that marks a character's speech or feeling in a story: the closing punctuation of a quoted utterance ('?"', '."', '!"'), a word naming an emotion (sad, sorry, disappointed, surprised), or a character name where speech is attributed. It stays low on the same words used outside speech or feeling, for example 'sad' as a plain attributive adjective or a name in a non-speech role.

rival_explanations: The pole fires on any token that is the highly predictable completion of the preceding local context, regardless of speech or feeling, so it would fire just as strongly on ' the', ' at' or ' of' inside predictable phrases in plain narration.
The pole fires on character names and story content words wherever they appear, regardless of dialogue or emotion, so it would fire on names and nouns even in plain descriptive narration.
The pole fires at clause and sentence boundaries, so it would peak on punctuation and clause-final tokens even in plain narration with no speech or feeling.
